metric.label: Lexical baseline
metric.description: Character n-gram cosine distance. This is a reproducible lexical baseline, not a semantic or faithfulness score.

units.leftText: The words of Amos, who was among the herdsmen of Tekoa, which he saw concerning Israel in the days of Uzziah king of Judah and in the days of Jeroboam the son of Joash, king of Israel, two years before the earthquake.
units.rightText: These are the words of Amos, who was among the sheepherders of Tekoa— what he saw concerning Israel two years before the earthquake, in the days when Uzziah was king of Judah and Jeroboam son of Jehoash was king of Israel.
rightNotes: 1:1 Hebrew Joash, a variant of Jehoash

units.leftText: He said: “The LORD will roar from Zion, and utter his voice from Jerusalem; and the pastures of the shepherds will mourn, and the top of Carmel will wither.”
units.rightText: He said: “The LORD roars from Zion and raises His voice from Jerusalem; the pastures of the shepherds mourn, and the summit of Carmel withers.”
leftNotes: 1:2 When rendered in ALL CAPITAL LETTERS, “LORD” or “GOD” is the translation of God’s Proper Name (Hebrew “יהוה*”, usually pronounced Yahweh).

units.leftText: The LORD says: “For three transgressions of Damascus, yes, for four, I will not turn away its punishment, because they have threshed Gilead with threshing instruments of iron;
units.rightText: This is what the LORD says: “For three transgressions of Damascus, even four, I will not revoke My judgment, because they threshed Gilead with sledges of iron.
rightNotes: 1:3 Or I will not revoke the punishment; Hebrew I will not revoke it; also in verses 6, 9, 11, and 13

units.leftText: but I will send a fire into the house of Hazael, and it will devour the palaces of Ben Hadad.
units.rightText: So I will send fire upon the house of Hazael to consume the citadels of Ben-hadad.

units.leftText: I will break the bar of Damascus, and cut off the inhabitant from the valley of Aven, and him who holds the scepter from the house of Eden; and the people of Syria shall go into captivity to Kir,” says the LORD.
units.rightText: I will break down the gates of Damascus; I will cut off the ruler from the Valley of Aven and the one who wields the scepter in Beth-eden. The people of Aram will be exiled to Kir,” says the LORD.

units.leftText: The LORD says: “For three transgressions of Gaza, yes, for four, I will not turn away its punishment, because they carried away captive the whole community, to deliver them up to Edom;
units.rightText: This is what the LORD says: “For three transgressions of Gaza, even four, I will not revoke My judgment, because they exiled a whole population, delivering them up to Edom.

units.leftText: but I will send a fire on the wall of Gaza, and it will devour its palaces.
units.rightText: So I will send fire upon the walls of Gaza, to consume its citadels.

units.leftText: I will cut off the inhabitant from Ashdod, and him who holds the scepter from Ashkelon; and I will turn my hand against Ekron; and the remnant of the Philistines will perish,” says the Lord GOD.
units.rightText: I will cut off the ruler of Ashdod and the one who wields the scepter in Ashkelon. I will turn My hand against Ekron, and the remnant of the Philistines will perish,” says the Lord GOD.

units.leftText: The LORD says: “For three transgressions of Tyre, yes, for four, I will not turn away its punishment; because they delivered up the whole community to Edom, and didn’t remember the brotherly covenant;
units.rightText: This is what the LORD says: “For three transgressions of Tyre, even four, I will not revoke My judgment, because they delivered up a whole congregation of exiles to Edom and broke a covenant of brotherhood.

units.leftText: but I will send a fire on the wall of Tyre, and it will devour its palaces.”
units.rightText: So I will send fire upon the walls of Tyre to consume its citadels.”

units.leftText: The LORD says: “For three transgressions of Edom, yes, for four, I will not turn away its punishment, because he pursued his brother with the sword and cast off all pity, and his anger raged continually, and he kept his wrath forever;
units.rightText: This is what the LORD says: “For three transgressions of Edom, even four, I will not revoke My judgment, because he pursued his brother with the sword and stifled all compassion; his anger raged continually, and his fury flamed incessantly.

units.leftText: but I will send a fire on Teman, and it will devour the palaces of Bozrah.”
units.rightText: So I will send fire upon Teman to consume the citadels of Bozrah.”

units.leftText: The LORD says: “For three transgressions of the children of Ammon, yes, for four, I will not turn away its punishment, because they have ripped open the pregnant women of Gilead, that they may enlarge their border.
units.rightText: This is what the LORD says: “For three transgressions of the Ammonites, even four, I will not revoke My judgment, because they ripped open the pregnant women of Gilead in order to enlarge their territory.

units.leftText: But I will kindle a fire in the wall of Rabbah, and it will devour its palaces, with shouting in the day of battle, with a storm in the day of the whirlwind;
units.rightText: So I will kindle a fire in the walls of Rabbah to consume its citadels amid war cries on the day of battle and a violent wind on the day of tempest.

units.leftText: and their king will go into captivity, he and his princes together,” says the LORD.
units.rightText: Their king will go into exile — he and his princes together,” says the LORD.
rightNotes: 1:15 Possibly Milcom will go into exile; Milcom, also called Molech, was god of the Ammonites; see Leviticus 18:21|LEV 18:21* and 1 Kings 11:7.

units.leftText: The LORD says: “For three transgressions of Moab, yes, for four, I will not turn away its punishment, because he burned the bones of the king of Edom into lime;
units.rightText: This is what the LORD says: “For three transgressions of Moab, even four, I will not revoke My judgment, because he burned to lime the bones of Edom’s king.
rightNotes: 2:1 Or I will not revoke the punishment; Hebrew I will not revoke it; also in verses 4 and 6

units.leftText: but I will send a fire on Moab, and it will devour the palaces of Kerioth; and Moab will die with tumult, with shouting, and with the sound of the trumpet;
units.rightText: So I will send fire against Moab to consume the citadels of Kerioth. Moab will die in tumult, amid war cries and the sound of the ram’s horn.

units.leftText: and I will cut off the judge from among them, and will kill all its princes with him,” says the LORD.
units.rightText: I will cut off the ruler of Moab and kill all the officials with him,” says the LORD.

units.leftText: The LORD says: “For three transgressions of Judah, yes, for four, I will not turn away its punishment, because they have rejected the LORD’s law, and have not kept his statutes, and their lies have led them astray, after which their fathers walked;
units.rightText: This is what the LORD says: “For three transgressions of Judah, even four, I will not revoke My judgment, because they reject the Law of the LORD and fail to keep His statutes; they are led astray by the lies in which their fathers walked.

units.leftText: but I will send a fire on Judah, and it will devour the palaces of Jerusalem.”
units.rightText: So I will send fire upon Judah to consume the citadels of Jerusalem.”

units.leftText: The LORD says: “For three transgressions of Israel, yes, for four, I will not turn away its punishment, because they have sold the righteous for silver, and the needy for a pair of sandals;
units.rightText: This is what the LORD says: “For three transgressions of Israel, even four, I will not revoke My judgment, because they sell the righteous for silver and the needy for a pair of sandals.

units.leftText: They trample the heads of the poor into the dust of the earth and deny justice to the oppressed. A man and his father use the same maiden, to profane my holy name.
units.rightText: They trample on the heads of the poor as on the dust of the earth; they push the needy out of their way. A man and his father have relations with the same girl and so profane My holy name.

units.leftText: They lay themselves down beside every altar on clothes taken in pledge. In the house of their God they drink the wine of those who have been fined.
units.rightText: They lie down beside every altar on garments taken in pledge. And in the house of their God, they drink wine obtained through fines.
rightNotes: 2:8 Or they drink the wine of those who have been fined

units.leftText: Yet I destroyed the Amorite before them, whose height was like the height of the cedars, and he was strong as the oaks; yet I destroyed his fruit from above, and his roots from beneath.
units.rightText: Yet it was I who destroyed the Amorite before them, though his height was like that of the cedars, and he was as strong as the oaks. Yet I destroyed his fruit above and his roots below.

units.leftText: Also I brought you up out of the land of Egypt and led you forty years in the wilderness, to possess the land of the Amorite.
units.rightText: And I brought you up from the land of Egypt and led you forty years in the wilderness, that you might take possession of the land of the Amorite.

units.leftText: I raised up some of your sons for prophets, and some of your young men for Nazirites. Isn’t this true, you children of Israel?” says the LORD.
units.rightText: I raised up prophets from your sons and Nazirites from your young men. Is this not true, O children of Israel?” declares the LORD.

units.leftText: “But you gave the Nazirites wine to drink, and commanded the prophets, saying, ‘Don’t prophesy!’
units.rightText: “But you made the Nazirites drink wine and commanded the prophets not to prophesy.

units.leftText: Behold, I will crush you in your place, as a cart crushes that is full of grain.
units.rightText: Behold, I am about to crush you in your place as with a cart full of grain.
leftNotes: 2:13 “Behold”, from “הִנֵּה*”, means look at, take notice, observe, see, or gaze at. It is often used as an interjection.

units.leftText: Flight will perish from the swift. The strong won’t strengthen his force. The mighty won’t deliver himself.
units.rightText: Escape will fail the swift, the strong will not prevail by his strength, and the mighty will not save his life.

units.leftText: He who handles the bow won’t stand. He who is swift of foot won’t escape. He who rides the horse won’t deliver himself.
units.rightText: The archer will not stand his ground, the fleet of foot will not escape, and the horseman will not save his life.

units.leftText: He who is courageous among the mighty will flee away naked on that day,” says the LORD.
units.rightText: Even the bravest of mighty men will flee naked on that day,” declares the LORD.

units.leftText: Hear this word that the LORD has spoken against you, children of Israel, against the whole family which I brought up out of the land of Egypt, saying:
units.rightText: Hear this word that the LORD has spoken against you, O children of Israel, against the whole family that I brought up out of the land of Egypt:

units.leftText: “I have chosen only you of all the families of the earth. Therefore I will punish you for all of your sins.”
units.rightText: “Only you have I known from all the families of the earth; therefore I will punish you for all your iniquities.”

units.leftText: Do two walk together, unless they have agreed?
units.rightText: Can two walk together without agreeing where to go?
rightNotes: 3:3 Or without an appointment to meet

units.leftText: Will a lion roar in the thicket, when he has no prey? Does a young lion cry out of his den, if he has caught nothing?
units.rightText: Does a lion roar in the forest when he has no prey? Does a young lion growl in his den if he has caught nothing?

units.leftText: Can a bird fall in a trap on the earth, where no snare is set for him? Does a snare spring up from the ground, when there is nothing to catch?
units.rightText: Does a bird land in a snare where no bait has been set? Does a trap spring from the ground when it has nothing to catch?

units.leftText: Does the trumpet alarm sound in a city, without the people being afraid? Does evil happen to a city, and the LORD hasn’t done it?
units.rightText: If a ram’s horn sounds in a city, do the people not tremble? If calamity comes to a city, has not the LORD caused it?

units.leftText: Surely the Lord GOD will do nothing, unless he reveals his secret to his servants the prophets.
units.rightText: Surely the Lord GOD does nothing without revealing His plan to His servants the prophets.

units.leftText: The lion has roared. Who will not fear? The Lord GOD has spoken. Who can but prophesy?
units.rightText: The lion has roared — who will not fear? The Lord GOD has spoken — who will not prophesy?

units.leftText: Proclaim in the palaces at Ashdod, and in the palaces in the land of Egypt, and say, “Assemble yourselves on the mountains of Samaria, and see what unrest is in her, and what oppression is among them.”
units.rightText: Proclaim to the citadels of Ashdod and to the citadels of Egypt: “Assemble on the mountains of Samaria; see the great unrest in the city and the acts of oppression in her midst.”

units.leftText: “Indeed they don’t know to do right,” says the LORD, “Who hoard plunder and loot in their palaces.”
units.rightText: “For they know not how to do right,” declares the LORD. “They store up violence and destruction in their citadels.”

units.leftText: Therefore the Lord GOD says: “An adversary will overrun the land; and he will pull down your strongholds, and your fortresses will be plundered.”
units.rightText: Therefore this is what the Lord GOD says: “An enemy will surround the land; he will pull down your strongholds and plunder your citadels.”

units.leftText: The LORD says: “As the shepherd rescues out of the mouth of the lion two legs, or a piece of an ear, so shall the children of Israel be rescued who sit in Samaria on the corner of a couch, and on the silken cushions of a bed.”
units.rightText: This is what the LORD says: “As the shepherd snatches from the mouth of the lion two legs or a piece of an ear, so the Israelites dwelling in Samaria will be rescued having just the corner of a bed or the cushion of a couch.
rightNotes: 3:12 Or so will the Israelites be snatched away, those who sit in Samaria on the edge of their beds and in Damascus on their couches

units.leftText: “Listen, and testify against the house of Jacob,” says the Lord GOD, the God of Armies.
units.rightText: Hear and testify against the house of Jacob, declares the Lord GOD, the God of Hosts.

units.leftText: “For in the day that I visit the transgressions of Israel on him, I will also visit the altars of Bethel; and the horns of the altar will be cut off, and fall to the ground.
units.rightText: On the day I punish Israel for their transgressions, I will visit destruction on the altars of Bethel; the horns of the altar will be cut off, and they will fall to the ground.

units.leftText: I will strike the winter house with the summer house; and the houses of ivory will perish, and the great houses will have an end,” says the LORD.
units.rightText: I will tear down the winter house along with the summer house; the houses of ivory will also perish, and the great houses will come to an end,” declares the LORD.

units.leftText: Listen to this word, you cows of Bashan, who are on the mountain of Samaria, who oppress the poor, who crush the needy, who tell their husbands, “Bring us drinks!”
units.rightText: Hear this word, you cows of Bashan on Mount Samaria, you women who oppress the poor and crush the needy, who say to your husbands, “Bring us more to drink.”

units.leftText: The Lord GOD has sworn by his holiness, “Behold, the days shall come on you that they will take you away with hooks, and the last of you with fish hooks.
units.rightText: The Lord GOD has sworn by His holiness: “Behold, the days are coming when you will be taken away with hooks, and your posterity with fishhooks.

units.leftText: You will go out at the breaks in the wall, everyone straight before her; and you will cast yourselves into Harmon,” says the LORD.
units.rightText: You will go out through broken walls, each one straight ahead of her, and you will be cast out toward Harmon, ” declares the LORD.

units.leftText: “Go to Bethel, and sin; to Gilgal, and sin more. Bring your sacrifices every morning, your tithes every three days,
units.rightText: “Go to Bethel and transgress; rebel even more at Gilgal! Bring your sacrifices every morning, your tithes every three days.

units.leftText: offer a sacrifice of thanksgiving of that which is leavened, and proclaim free will offerings and brag about them; for this pleases you, you children of Israel,” says the Lord GOD.
units.rightText: Offer leavened bread as a thank offering, and loudly proclaim your freewill offerings. For that is what you children of Israel love to do,” declares the Lord GOD.

units.leftText: “I also have given you cleanness of teeth in all your cities, and lack of bread in every town; yet you haven’t returned to me,” says the LORD.
units.rightText: “I afflicted all your cities with cleanness of teeth and all your towns with lack of bread, yet you did not return to Me,” declares the LORD.

units.leftText: “I also have withheld the rain from you, when there were yet three months to the harvest; and I caused it to rain on one city, and caused it not to rain on another city. One field was rained on, and the field where it didn’t rain withered.
units.rightText: “I also withheld the rain from you when the harvest was three months away. I sent rain on one city but withheld it from another. One field received rain; another without rain withered.

units.leftText: So two or three cities staggered to one city to drink water, and were not satisfied; yet you haven’t returned to me,” says the LORD.
units.rightText: People staggered from city to city for water to drink, but they were not satisfied; yet you did not return to Me,” declares the LORD.

units.leftText: “I struck you with blight and mildew many times in your gardens and your vineyards, and the swarming locusts have devoured your fig trees and your olive trees; yet you haven’t returned to me,” says the LORD.
units.rightText: “I struck you with blight and mildew in your growing gardens and vineyards; the locust devoured your fig and olive trees, yet you did not return to Me,” declares the LORD.

units.leftText: “I sent plagues among you like I did Egypt. I have slain your young men with the sword, and have carried away your horses. I filled your nostrils with the stench of your camp, yet you haven’t returned to me,” says the LORD.
units.rightText: “I sent plagues among you like those of Egypt; I killed your young men with the sword, along with your captured horses. I filled your nostrils with the stench of your camp, yet you did not return to Me,” declares the LORD.

units.leftText: “I have overthrown some of you, as when God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah, and you were like a burning stick plucked out of the fire; yet you haven’t returned to me,” says the LORD.
units.rightText: “Some of you I overthrew as I overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah, and you were like a firebrand snatched from a blaze, yet you did not return to Me,” declares the LORD.

units.leftText: “Therefore I will do this to you, Israel; because I will do this to you, prepare to meet your God, Israel.
units.rightText: “Therefore, that is what I will do to you, O Israel, and since I will do this to you, prepare to meet your God, O Israel!

units.leftText: For, behold, he who forms the mountains, creates the wind, declares to man what is his thought, who makes the morning darkness, and treads on the high places of the earth: The LORD, the God of Armies, is his name.”
units.rightText: For behold, He who forms the mountains, who creates the wind and reveals His thoughts to man, who turns the dawn to darkness and strides on the heights of the earth— the LORD, the God of Hosts, is His name.”

units.leftText: Listen to this word which I take up for a lamentation over you, O house of Israel:
units.rightText: Hear this word, O house of Israel, this lamentation I take up against you:

units.leftText: “The virgin of Israel has fallen; She shall rise no more. She is cast down on her land; there is no one to raise her up.”
units.rightText: “Fallen is Virgin Israel, never to rise again. She lies abandoned on her land, with no one to raise her up.”

units.leftText: For the Lord GOD says: “The city that went out a thousand shall have a hundred left, and that which went out one hundred shall have ten left to the house of Israel.”
units.rightText: This is what the Lord GOD says: “The city that marches out a thousand strong will have but a hundred left, and the one that marches out a hundred strong will have but ten left in the house of Israel.” A Call to Repentance (Joel 1:13–20|JOL 1:13-20*; Zephaniah 2:1–3|ZEP 2:1-3*; Luke 13:1–5|LUK 13:1-5*)

units.leftText: For the LORD says to the house of Israel: “Seek me, and you will live;
units.rightText: For this is what the LORD says to the house of Israel: “Seek Me and live!

units.leftText: but don’t seek Bethel, nor enter into Gilgal, and don’t pass to Beersheba; for Gilgal shall surely go into captivity, and Bethel shall come to nothing.
units.rightText: Do not seek Bethel or go to Gilgal; do not journey to Beersheba, for Gilgal will surely go into exile, and Bethel will come to nothing.
rightNotes: 5:5 Hebrew to Aven, a reference to Beth-aven, a derogatory term for Bethel; see Hosea 4:15|HOS 4:15*.

units.leftText: Seek the LORD, and you will live, lest he break out like fire in the house of Joseph, and it devour, and there be no one to quench it in Bethel.
units.rightText: Seek the LORD and live, or He will sweep like fire through the house of Joseph; it will devour everything, with no one at Bethel to extinguish it.

units.leftText: You who turn justice to wormwood, and cast down righteousness to the earth!
units.rightText: There are those who turn justice into wormwood and cast righteousness to the ground.

units.leftText: Seek him who made the Pleiades and Orion, and turns the shadow of death into the morning, and makes the day dark with night; who calls for the waters of the sea, and pours them out on the surface of the earth, the LORD is his name,
units.rightText: He who made the Pleiades and Orion, who turns darkness into dawn and darkens day into night, who summons the waters of the sea and pours them over the face of the earth — the LORD is His name —

units.leftText: who brings sudden destruction on the strong, so that destruction comes on the fortress.
units.rightText: He flashes destruction on the strong, so that fury comes upon the stronghold.

units.leftText: They hate him who reproves in the gate, and they abhor him who speaks blamelessly.
units.rightText: There are those who hate the one who reproves in the gate and despise him who speaks with integrity.

units.leftText: Therefore, because you trample on the poor and take taxes from him of wheat, you have built houses of cut stone, but you will not dwell in them. You have planted pleasant vineyards, but you shall not drink their wine.
units.rightText: Therefore, because you trample on the poor and exact from him a tax of grain, you will never live in the stone houses you have built; you will never drink the wine from the lush vineyards you have planted.

units.leftText: For I know how many are your offenses, and how great are your sins— you who afflict the just, who take a bribe, and who turn away the needy in the courts.
units.rightText: For I know that your transgressions are many and your sins are numerous. You oppress the righteous by taking bribes; you deprive the poor of justice in the gate.

units.leftText: Therefore a prudent person keeps silent in such a time, for it is an evil time.
units.rightText: Therefore, the prudent keep silent in such times, for the days are evil.

units.leftText: Seek good, and not evil, that you may live; and so the LORD, the God of Armies, will be with you, as you say.
units.rightText: Seek good, not evil, so that you may live. And the LORD, the God of Hosts, will be with you, as you have claimed.

units.leftText: Hate evil, love good, and establish justice in the courts. It may be that the LORD, the God of Armies, will be gracious to the remnant of Joseph.”
units.rightText: Hate evil and love good; establish justice in the gate. Perhaps the LORD, the God of Hosts, will be gracious to the remnant of Joseph.” Woe to Rebellious Israel (Acts 7:39–43|ACT 7:39-43*)

units.leftText: Therefore the LORD, the God of Armies, the Lord, says: “Wailing will be in all the wide ways. They will say in all the streets, ‘Alas! Alas!’ They will call the farmer to mourning, and those who are skillful in lamentation to wailing.
units.rightText: Therefore this is what the LORD, the God of Hosts, the Lord, says: “There will be wailing in all the public squares and cries of ‘Alas! Alas!’ in all the streets. The farmer will be summoned to mourn, and the mourners to wail.

units.leftText: In all vineyards there will be wailing, for I will pass through the middle of you,” says the LORD.
units.rightText: There will be wailing in all the vineyards, for I will pass through your midst,” says the LORD.

units.leftText: “Woe to you who desire the day of the LORD! Why do you long for the day of the LORD? It is darkness, and not light.
units.rightText: Woe to you who long for the Day of the LORD! What will the Day of the LORD be for you? It will be darkness and not light.

units.leftText: As if a man fled from a lion, and a bear met him; or he went into the house and leaned his hand on the wall, and a snake bit him.
units.rightText: It will be like a man who flees from a lion, only to encounter a bear, or who enters his house and rests his hand against the wall, only to be bitten by a snake.

units.leftText: Won’t the day of the LORD be darkness, and not light? Even very dark, and no brightness in it?
units.rightText: Will not the Day of the LORD be darkness and not light, even gloom with no brightness in it?

units.leftText: I hate, I despise your feasts, and I can’t stand your solemn assemblies.
units.rightText: “I hate, I despise your feasts! I cannot stand the stench of your solemn assemblies.

units.leftText: Yes, though you offer me your burnt offerings and meal offerings, I will not accept them; neither will I regard the peace offerings of your fat animals.
units.rightText: Even though you offer Me burnt offerings and grain offerings, I will not accept them; for your peace offerings of fattened cattle I will have no regard.

units.leftText: Take away from me the noise of your songs! I will not listen to the music of your harps.
units.rightText: Take away from Me the noise of your songs! I will not listen to the music of your harps.

units.leftText: But let justice roll on like rivers, and righteousness like a mighty stream.
units.rightText: But let justice roll on like a river, and righteousness like an ever-flowing stream.

units.leftText: “Did you bring to me sacrifices and offerings in the wilderness forty years, house of Israel?
units.rightText: Did you bring Me sacrifices and offerings forty years in the wilderness, O house of Israel?

units.leftText: You also carried the tent of your king and the shrine of your images, the star of your god, which you made for yourselves.
units.rightText: You have taken along Sakkuth your king and Kaiwan your star god, the idols you made for yourselves.
rightNotes: 5:26 LXX You have taken along the tabernacle of Molech and the star of your god Rephan

units.leftText: Therefore I will cause you to go into captivity beyond Damascus,” says the LORD, whose name is the God of Armies.
units.rightText: Therefore I will send you into exile beyond Damascus,” says the LORD, whose name is the God of Hosts.

units.leftText: Woe to those who are at ease in Zion, and to those who are secure on the mountain of Samaria, the notable men of the chief of the nations, to whom the house of Israel come!
units.rightText: Woe to those at ease in Zion and those secure on Mount Samaria, the distinguished ones of the foremost nation, to whom the house of Israel comes.

units.leftText: Go to Calneh, and see. From there go to Hamath the great. Then go down to Gath of the Philistines. Are they better than these kingdoms? Is their border greater than your border?
units.rightText: Cross over to Calneh and see; go from there to the great Hamath; then go down to Gath of the Philistines. Are you better than these kingdoms? Is their territory larger than yours?

units.leftText: Alas for you who put far away the evil day, and cause the seat of violence to come near,
units.rightText: You dismiss the day of calamity and bring near a reign of violence.

units.leftText: who lie on beds of ivory, and stretch themselves on their couches, and eat the lambs out of the flock, and the calves out of the middle of the stall,
units.rightText: You lie on beds inlaid with ivory, and lounge upon your couches. You dine on lambs from the flock and calves from the stall.

units.leftText: who strum on the strings of a harp, who invent for themselves instruments of music, like David;
units.rightText: You improvise songs on the harp like David and invent your own musical instruments.

units.leftText: who drink wine in bowls, and anoint themselves with the best oils, but they are not grieved for the affliction of Joseph.
units.rightText: You drink wine by the bowlful and anoint yourselves with the finest oils, but you fail to grieve over the ruin of Joseph.

units.leftText: Therefore they will now go captive with the first who go captive. The feasting and lounging will end.
units.rightText: Therefore, you will now go into exile as the first of the captives, and your feasting and lounging will come to an end. The Pride of Israel

units.leftText: “The Lord GOD has sworn by himself,” says the LORD, the God of Armies: “I abhor the pride of Jacob, and detest his fortresses. Therefore I will deliver up the city with all that is in it.
units.rightText: The Lord GOD has sworn by Himself— the LORD, the God of Hosts, has declared: “I abhor Jacob’s pride and detest his citadels, so I will deliver up the city and everything in it.”

units.leftText: It will happen that if ten men remain in one house, they will die.
units.rightText: And if there are ten men left in one house, they too will die.

units.leftText: “When a man’s relative carries him, even he who burns him, to bring bodies out of the house, and asks him who is in the innermost parts of the house, ‘Is there yet any with you?’ And he says, ‘No;’ then he will say, ‘Hush! Indeed we must not mention the LORD’s name.’
units.rightText: And when the relative who is to burn the bodies picks them up to remove them from the house, he will call to one inside, “Is anyone else with you?” “None,” that person will answer. “Silence,” the relative will retort, “for the name of the LORD must not be invoked.”
rightNotes: 6:10 Or to make a funeral fire to honor the dead

units.leftText: “For, behold, the LORD commands, and the great house will be smashed to pieces, and the little house into bits.
units.rightText: For the LORD gives a command: “The great house will be smashed to pieces, and the small house to rubble.”

units.leftText: Do horses run on the rocky crags? Does one plow there with oxen? But you have turned justice into poison, and the fruit of righteousness into bitterness,
units.rightText: “Do horses gallop on the cliffs? Does one plow the sea with oxen? But you have turned justice into poison and the fruit of righteousness into wormwood—

units.leftText: you who rejoice in a thing of nothing, who say, ‘Haven’t we taken for ourselves horns by our own strength?’
units.rightText: you who rejoice in Lo-debar and say, ‘Did we not take Karnaim by our own strength?’
rightNotes: 6:13 Karnaim means horn, a symbol of strength.

units.leftText: For, behold, I will raise up against you a nation, house of Israel,” says the LORD, the God of Armies; “and they will afflict you from the entrance of Hamath to the brook of the Arabah.”
units.rightText: For behold, I will raise up a nation against you, O house of Israel,” declares the LORD, the God of Hosts, “and they will oppress you from Lebo-hamath to the Brook of the Arabah.”

units.leftText: Thus the Lord GOD showed me: behold, he formed locusts in the beginning of the shooting up of the latter growth; and behold, it was the latter growth after the king’s harvest.
units.rightText: This is what the Lord GOD showed me: He was preparing swarms of locusts just after the king’s harvest, as the late spring crop was coming up.
rightNotes: 7:1 LXX A swarm of locusts coming from the east; and, behold, one grasshopper, king Gog.

units.leftText: When they finished eating the grass of the land, then I said, “Lord GOD, forgive, I beg you! How could Jacob stand? For he is small.”
units.rightText: And when the locusts had eaten every green plant in the land, I said, “Lord GOD, please forgive! How will Jacob survive, since he is so small?”

units.leftText: The LORD relented concerning this. “It shall not be,” says the LORD.
units.rightText: So the LORD relented from this plan. “It will not happen,” He said.

units.leftText: Thus the Lord GOD showed me: behold, the Lord GOD called for judgment by fire; and it dried up the great deep, and would have devoured the land.
units.rightText: This is what the Lord GOD showed me: The Lord GOD was calling for judgment by fire. It consumed the great deep and devoured the land.

units.leftText: Then I said, “Lord GOD, stop, I beg you! How could Jacob stand? For he is small.”
units.rightText: Then I said, “Lord GOD, please stop! How will Jacob survive, since he is so small?”

units.leftText: The LORD relented concerning this. “This also shall not be,” says the Lord GOD.
units.rightText: So the LORD relented from this plan. “It will not happen either,” said the Lord GOD.

units.leftText: Thus he showed me: behold, the Lord stood beside a wall made by a plumb line, with a plumb line in his hand.
units.rightText: This is what He showed me: Behold, the Lord was standing by a wall true to plumb, with a plumb line in His hand.

units.leftText: The LORD said to me, “Amos, what do you see?” I said, “A plumb line.” Then the Lord said, “Behold, I will set a plumb line in the middle of my people Israel. I will not again pass by them any more.
units.rightText: “Amos, what do you see?” asked the LORD. “A plumb line,” I replied. “Behold,” said the Lord, “I am setting a plumb line among My people Israel; I will no longer spare them:

units.leftText: The high places of Isaac will be desolate, the sanctuaries of Israel will be laid waste; and I will rise against the house of Jeroboam with the sword.”
units.rightText: The high places of Isaac will be deserted, and the sanctuaries of Israel will be laid waste; and I will rise up against the house of Jeroboam with My sword.” Amaziah Accuses Amos

units.leftText: Then Amaziah the priest of Bethel sent to Jeroboam king of Israel, saying, “Amos has conspired against you in the middle of the house of Israel. The land is not able to bear all his words.
units.rightText: Then Amaziah the priest of Bethel sent word to Jeroboam king of Israel, saying, “Amos has conspired against you in the midst of the house of Israel. The land cannot bear all his words,

units.leftText: For Amos says, ‘Jeroboam will die by the sword, and Israel shall surely be led away captive out of his land.’”
units.rightText: for this is what Amos has said: ‘Jeroboam will die by the sword, and Israel will surely go into exile, away from their homeland.’”

units.leftText: Amaziah also said to Amos, “You seer, go, flee away into the land of Judah, and there eat bread, and prophesy there,
units.rightText: And Amaziah said to Amos, “Go away, you seer! Flee to the land of Judah; earn your bread there and do your prophesying there.

units.leftText: but don’t prophesy again any more at Bethel; for it is the king’s sanctuary, and it is a royal house!”
units.rightText: But never prophesy at Bethel again, because it is the sanctuary of the king and the temple of the kingdom.”

units.leftText: Then Amos answered Amaziah, “I was no prophet, neither was I a prophet’s son, but I was a herdsman, and a farmer of sycamore figs;
units.rightText: “I was not a prophet,” Amos replied, “nor was I the son of a prophet; rather, I was a herdsman and a tender of sycamore-fig trees.
rightNotes: 7:14 Or nor am I the son

units.leftText: and the LORD took me from following the flock, and the LORD said to me, ‘Go, prophesy to my people Israel.’
units.rightText: But the LORD took me from following the flock and said to me, ‘Go, prophesy to My people Israel.’

units.leftText: Now therefore listen to the LORD’s word: ‘You say, Don’t prophesy against Israel, and don’t preach against the house of Isaac.’
units.rightText: Now, therefore, hear the word of the LORD. You say: ‘Do not prophesy against Israel; do not preach against the house of Isaac.’

units.leftText: Therefore the LORD says: ‘Your wife shall be a prostitute in the city, and your sons and your daughters shall fall by the sword, and your land shall be divided by line; and you yourself shall die in a land that is unclean, and Israel shall surely be led away captive out of his land.’”
units.rightText: Therefore this is what the LORD says: ‘Your wife will become a prostitute in the city, and your sons and daughters will fall by the sword. Your land will be divided by a measuring line, and you yourself will die on pagan soil. And Israel will surely go into exile, away from their homeland.’”

units.leftText: Thus the Lord GOD showed me: behold, a basket of summer fruit.
units.rightText: This is what the Lord GOD showed me: I saw a basket of summer fruit.
rightNotes: 8:1 Or ripe fruit; also in verse 2

units.leftText: He said, “Amos, what do you see?” I said, “A basket of summer fruit.” Then the LORD said to me, “The end has come on my people Israel. I will not again pass by them any more.
units.rightText: “Amos, what do you see?” He asked. “A basket of summer fruit,” I replied. So the LORD said to me, “The end has come for My people Israel; I will no longer spare them.”

units.leftText: The songs of the temple will be wailing in that day,” says the Lord GOD. “The dead bodies will be many. In every place they will throw them out with silence.
units.rightText: “In that day,” declares the Lord GOD, “the songs of the temple will turn to wailing. Many will be the corpses, strewn in silence everywhere!”

units.leftText: Hear this, you who desire to swallow up the needy, and cause the poor of the land to fail,
units.rightText: Hear this, you who trample the needy, who do away with the poor of the land,

units.leftText: saying, ‘When will the new moon be gone, that we may sell grain? And the Sabbath, that we may market wheat, making the ephah small, and the shekel large, and dealing falsely with balances of deceit;
units.rightText: asking, “When will the New Moon be over, that we may sell grain? When will the Sabbath end, that we may market wheat? Let us reduce the ephah and increase the shekel; let us cheat with dishonest scales.
leftNotes: 8:5 1 ephah is about 22 liters or about 2/3 of a bushel
8:5 a normal shekel is about 10 grams or about 0.35 ounces.
rightNotes: 8:5 Or Let us reduce the measure and increase the price

units.leftText: that we may buy the poor for silver, and the needy for a pair of sandals, and sell the sweepings with the wheat?’”
units.rightText: Let us buy the poor with silver and the needy for a pair of sandals, selling even the chaff with the wheat!”

units.leftText: The LORD has sworn by the pride of Jacob, “Surely I will never forget any of their works.
units.rightText: The LORD has sworn by the Pride of Jacob: “I will never forget any of their deeds.

units.leftText: Won’t the land tremble for this, and everyone mourn who dwells in it? Yes, it will rise up wholly like the River; and it will be stirred up and sink again, like the River of Egypt.
units.rightText: Will not the land quake for this, and all its dwellers mourn? All of it will swell like the Nile; it will surge and then subside like the Nile in Egypt.

units.leftText: It will happen in that day,” says the Lord GOD, “that I will cause the sun to go down at noon, and I will darken the earth in the clear day.
units.rightText: And in that day, declares the Lord GOD, I will make the sun go down at noon, and I will darken the earth in the daytime.

units.leftText: I will turn your feasts into mourning, and all your songs into lamentation; and I will make you wear sackcloth on all your bodies, and baldness on every head. I will make it like the mourning for an only son, and its end like a bitter day.
units.rightText: I will turn your feasts into mourning and all your songs into lamentation. I will cause everyone to wear sackcloth and every head to be shaved. I will make it like a time of mourning for an only son, and its outcome like a bitter day.

units.leftText: Behold, the days come,” says the Lord GOD, “that I will send a famine in the land, not a famine of bread, nor a thirst for water, but of hearing the LORD’s words.
units.rightText: Behold, the days are coming, declares the Lord GOD, when I will send a famine on the land — not a famine of bread or a thirst for water, but a famine of hearing the words of the LORD.

units.leftText: They will wander from sea to sea, and from the north even to the east; they will run back and forth to seek the LORD’s word, and will not find it.
units.rightText: People will stagger from sea to sea and roam from north to east, seeking the word of the LORD, but they will not find it.

units.leftText: In that day the beautiful virgins and the young men will faint for thirst.
units.rightText: In that day the lovely young women — the young men as well — will faint from thirst.

units.leftText: Those who swear by the sin of Samaria, and say, ‘As your god, Dan, lives,’ and, ‘As the way of Beersheba lives,’ they will fall, and never rise up again.”
units.rightText: Those who swear by the guilt of Samaria and say, ‘As surely as your god lives, O Dan,’ or, ‘As surely as the way of Beersheba lives’— they will fall, never to rise again.”

units.leftText: I saw the Lord standing beside the altar, and he said, “Strike the tops of the pillars, that the thresholds may shake. Break them in pieces on the head of all of them. I will kill the last of them with the sword. Not one of them will flee away. Not one of them will escape.
units.rightText: I saw the Lord standing beside the altar, and He said: “Strike the tops of the pillars so that the thresholds shake. Topple them on the heads of all the people, and I will kill the rest with the sword. None of those who flee will get away; none of the fugitives will escape.

units.leftText: Though they dig into Sheol, there my hand will take them; and though they climb up to heaven, there I will bring them down.
units.rightText: Though they dig down to Sheol, from there My hand will take them; and though they climb up to heaven, from there I will pull them down.
leftNotes: 9:2 Sheol is the place of the dead.

units.leftText: Though they hide themselves in the top of Carmel, I will search and take them out from there; and though they be hidden from my sight in the bottom of the sea, there I will command the serpent, and it will bite them.
units.rightText: Though they hide themselves atop Carmel, there I will track them and seize them; and though they hide from Me at the bottom of the sea, there I will command the serpent to bite them.
rightNotes: 9:3 Hebrew nachash; translated in most cases as snake

units.leftText: Though they go into captivity before their enemies, there I will command the sword, and it will kill them. I will set my eyes on them for evil, and not for good.
units.rightText: Though they are driven by their enemies into captivity, there I will command the sword to slay them. I will fix My eyes upon them for harm and not for good.”

units.leftText: For the Lord, the GOD of Armies, is he who touches the land and it melts, and all who dwell in it will mourn; and it will rise up wholly like the River, and will sink again, like the River of Egypt.
units.rightText: The Lord GOD of Hosts, He who touches the earth and it melts, and all its dwellers mourn — all the land rises like the Nile, then sinks like the river of Egypt —
leftNotes: 9:5 When rendered in ALL CAPITAL LETTERS, “LORD” or “GOD” is the translation of God’s Proper Name (Hebrew “יהוה*”, usually pronounced Yahweh).

units.leftText: It is he who builds his rooms in the heavens, and has founded his vault on the earth; he who calls for the waters of the sea, and pours them out on the surface of the earth—the LORD is his name.
units.rightText: He builds His upper rooms in the heavens and founds His vault upon the earth. He summons the waters of the sea and pours them over the face of the earth. The LORD is His name.

units.leftText: Are you not like the children of the Ethiopians to me, children of Israel?” says the LORD. “Haven’t I brought up Israel out of the land of Egypt, and the Philistines from Caphtor, and the Syrians from Kir?
units.rightText: “Are you not like the Cushites to Me, O children of Israel?” declares the LORD. “Did I not bring Israel up from the land of Egypt, the Philistines from Caphtor, and the Arameans from Kir?
rightNotes: 9:7 That is, people from the upper Nile region

units.leftText: Behold, the eyes of the Lord GOD are on the sinful kingdom, and I will destroy it from off the surface of the earth, except that I will not utterly destroy the house of Jacob,” says the LORD.
units.rightText: Surely the eyes of the Lord GOD are on the sinful kingdom, and I will destroy it from the face of the earth. Yet I will not utterly destroy the house of Jacob,” declares the LORD.

units.leftText: “For behold, I will command, and I will sift the house of Israel among all the nations as grain is sifted in a sieve, yet not the least kernel will fall on the earth.
units.rightText: “For surely I will give the command, and I will shake the house of Israel among all the nations as grain is sifted in a sieve; but not a pebble will reach the ground.

units.leftText: All the sinners of my people will die by the sword, who say, ‘Evil won’t overtake nor meet us.’
units.rightText: All the sinners among My people will die by the sword — all those who say, ‘Disaster will never draw near or confront us.’” A Promise of Restoration (Acts 15:5–21|ACT 15:5-21*)

units.leftText: In that day I will raise up the tent of David who is fallen and close up its breaches, and I will raise up its ruins, and I will build it as in the days of old,
units.rightText: “In that day I will restore the fallen tent of David. I will repair its gaps, restore its ruins, and rebuild it as in the days of old,

units.leftText: that they may possess the remnant of Edom and all the nations who are called by my name,” says the LORD who does this.
units.rightText: that they may possess the remnant of Edom and all the nations that bear My name,” declares the LORD, who will do this.
rightNotes: 9:12 Hebrew; LXX that the remnant of men, and all the nations that bear My name, may earnestly seek Me; cited in Acts 15:16–18|ACT 15:16-18*

units.leftText: “Behold, the days come,” says the LORD, “that the plowman shall overtake the reaper, and the one treading grapes him who sows seed; and sweet wine will drip from the mountains, and flow from the hills.
units.rightText: “Behold, the days are coming,” declares the LORD, “when the plowman will overtake the reaper and the treader of grapes, the sower of seed. The mountains will drip with sweet wine, with which all the hills will flow.

units.leftText: I will bring my people Israel back from captivity, and they will rebuild the ruined cities, and inhabit them; and they will plant vineyards, and drink wine from them. They shall also make gardens, and eat their fruit.
units.rightText: I will restore My people Israel from captivity; they will rebuild and inhabit the ruined cities. They will plant vineyards and drink their wine; they will make gardens and eat their fruit.
rightNotes: 9:14 Or restore the fortunes of My people Israel

units.leftText: I will plant them on their land, and they will no more be plucked up out of their land which I have given them,” says the LORD your God.
units.rightText: I will firmly plant them in their own land, never again to be uprooted from the land that I have given them,” says the LORD your God.
